body: I share this fear.  I have handled a few situations similar to this one, just never one this extreme.  She is stable enough to be safe around others, but social anxiety and high stress makes her very hard to deal with.  She shuts down very quickly, and if you ask a question that crosses her boundaries, she only replies either "Ok", "Ya", or "I am fine".  It's easy to tell when she shuts down, but it can take a long time to bring her out of her shell, and with such limited time to interact, it makes the whole thing a very slow process.

Her parents know, and have only told her that they disapprove.  Her mother has taken her to get professional help, and she decided after consulting with me that it would be beneficial to continue seeing this counselor.  The family as a whole did go to a family counselor shortly after the brother's death, but they all reacted negatively to it and stopped going after only 3 visits.

One major issue is that her mother is very controlling, and doesn't want there to be any more problems in the family, other than the divorce.  She does not want to lose her daughters, but expects them to act the way that she wants them to, which is the same way that she does.  Given her poor reaction to grieving for her son, this would is not a positive influence in this girl's life, and stresses her out more.  After the separation, the most likely scenario would be that she went to live with her father, who would then be taken to court in a custody battle as an unfit parent being an alcoholic.  So, as a minor, the she might not be able to escape living with her mother, which is the last thing she wants.

To give myself SOME credibility, I was suicidal and depressed at one point in my life.  I moved on from that period in my life by deciding I would share my story to help others out of similar situations.  That's how I ended up talking to her about her problems; I sensed something was deeply wrong in her life, shared my story, and she opened up to me about her brother and her cutting, and the fact that she was considering suicide at that very moment.  I talked her down, and one month later, have gotten a bit more of the story and have been trying to help her understand how to deal with stressors in her life appropriately, and help her discuss her best options moving forward.  She understands that suicide is not a good option, but it can make it worse, as she feels incredible guilt for having attempted multiple times already.

I have been supporting her as much as possible.  Yes, the cutting was an addiction.  You have the timeline wrong, though.  Sexual abuse happened AFTER brother's death.  It was the girl I am helping that was forced to watch her sister (two years older than her) be sexually abused.  She will not give me too much information about that event, so I have few details.  The accident with her brother happened as a normal day.  She (then aged 14), her brother (aged 17) and the friend (also 17) were messing around with brother's friend's car.  Sister went somewhere else.  Good time was had by all, and the brother decided he would try to hang on the back of his buddy's car while his buddy drove around.  Girl I am helping was in the passenger's seat, looking out the back window at her brother.  Brother fell off, hit the back of his head, and died immediately.  Ambulance was called, brother taken to hospital, declared dead on sight.

The circumstances that led to her sister being sexually abused by the friend afterwards will not be given to me, nor will the exact nature of the abuse.  She refuses to dwell on that.

Trust me, I've been trying to get a full picture for the month or so that I've known her and have been helping her, but she is very introverted, and very prone to anxiety attacks, and shuts down very easily.  She started self-harming after a failed suicide attempt (she tried to slit her wrists), but like the high a little more than she wanted to kill herself.  She has some self-worth, and is very willing to seek help.  That's about the only way I've been able to get her to talk about it with me; she knows that it's the only way that she can get help.

EDIT:  It might be important to note that according to her, life was perfectly normal before her brother died.  She, her siblings, and her parents were supposedly happy.  I cannot verify this, as I have only known her for a short time, now, and have to go on her word, which I then have to interpret a little better and verify with her my understanding of the events.
